value.body: An occupational health nurse looks after the health of workers at a factory, plant, mine, construction site or large office. Employers include manufacturing companies, industrial plants and occupational health service providers. A typical day involves handling injuries and illness at the on-site health centre, supporting periodic medical check-ups with the factory medical officer, and maintaining records.

items.label: Registration
items.value: State Nursing Council registration commonly required

items.label: Works with
items.value: Factory medical officer and safety (EHS) team

value.title: How you get in
value.body: Industrial employers and occupational health providers hire registered nurses, often preferring some emergency or hospital experience. A short certificate in occupational health or industrial first aid can help.

value.title: At a glance
items: Postings may be at industrial sites away from cities, sometimes in shifts.
Next roles: senior occupational health nurse, health and safety coordinator.
